## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(trail): add --json to trail show, pin the title+body update split

`entire trail show` had no machine-readable output, so an agent could only
read a trail through the human view. It now takes --json and prints one
trail object — the same shape as an entry of `trail list --json`, so both
feed the same parser. The description comes from the detail endpoint the
same way the text view resolves it, and the "-- no description provided --"
placeholder stays out of the JSON: an empty description is an empty string.
A failed description fetch still only warns, and the warning goes to stderr,
so stdout stays parseable.

`entire trail update --title X --body Y` already worked: the server rejects
body and metadata in one PATCH ("Body updates cannot be combined with
metadata updates"), and splitTrailUpdate sends them as two. But nothing
tested that end to end, and splitTrailUpdate decided "this is metadata" by
listing the field names by hand. Adding a metadata field without extending
that list makes the whole update vanish — hasMeta stays false, no PATCH is
sent, and the command still prints success. It now walks the struct
reflectively instead, so a field added later (trail 787's branch rename)
counts as metadata on its own, and a test iterates the struct to keep it
that way.

Also extracts runTrailShowWithClient and runTrailUpdateWithClient so both
paths can be driven against a test server, matching runTrailListAllWithClient.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Two small `entire trail` gaps.

## 1. `entire trail show` had no JSON output

An agent could only read a trail through the human view. `trail show` now takes
`--json` and prints one trail object — the same shape as an entry of
`trail list --json`, so both feed the same parser.

Details that matter:

- The description comes from the detail endpoint (`body_document.text_snapshot`)
  the same way the text view resolves it, with the list body as fallback.
- The `-- no description provided --` placeholder is display text, not data, so
  it never reaches the JSON: an empty description is an empty string.
- A failed description fetch still only warns, and the warning goes to stderr,
  so stdout stays parseable.

## 2. `trail update --title X --body Y` in one call

This already worked on main. The server rejects body and metadata in one PATCH
("Body updates cannot be combined with metadata updates"), and
`splitTrailUpdate` has been sending them as two PATCHes since
c74ff3cc9 (2026-07-10). If you hit a rejection, you were on a build older than
that — `entire version` reports `dev` for a local build, so it is easy to miss.

What was actually missing was protection. Two things:

- Nothing tested the split end to end. There is now a test that drives the whole
  update path against a server reproducing the real rejection rule, so the
  two-PATCH behaviour is pinned, plus one covering the non-atomic half (the
  metadata PATCH lands, the body PATCH fails, and the error says the metadata
  already applied).
- `splitTrailUpdate` decided "this is metadata" by listing the field names by
  hand. Add a metadata field and forget that list, and the whole update
  vanishes: `hasMeta` stays false, no PATCH is sent, and the command still
  prints success. It now walks `TrailUpdateRequest` reflectively, and a test
  iterates the struct so every non-body field has to count as metadata.

## Checked against trail 787

787 (`feat/trail-update-branch`) adds `--set-branch`, which sends a new `branch`
field — exactly the case the hand-written list would have dropped. I resolved
the merge locally in a throwaway branch and ran it: `--set-branch new/branch
--body "text"` sends `{"branch":"new/branch"}` then `{"body":"new body"}`, two
PATCHes, both accepted, with no extra code on this side. The reflective check
picks the new field up on its own.

Two notes for whoever lands 787:

- It already conflicts with main today, before this change — its base predates
  the assignee/reviewer/type/priority work and the split itself. Its
  `runTrailUpdate` does a single PATCH carrying body and metadata together, so
  the resolution has to keep main's split rather than 787's single call.
- 787 renames the success line from `Updated trail for branch <branch>` to
  `Updated trail #<n>`, so `TestRunTrailUpdateSendsTitleAndBodyAsSeparatePatches`
  needs that one string updated. The PATCH assertions pass unchanged.

## Also

Extracts `runTrailShowWithClient` and `runTrailUpdateWithClient` so both paths
can be driven against a test server, matching the existing
`runTrailListAllWithClient`.
